answer: In an orchard-monitoring agent market, each worker identity must lock $100 for 30 days to accept one concurrent job; extra identities grant no unbonded capacity. Even at the seasonal nadir in demand, the lock remains, so the market is no haven for cheap sybils: an attacker seeking 1,000 worker slots must immobilize $100,000. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes fake capacity cost as much collateral as real capacity.
